title: Language Model Fine-Tuning on Scaled Survey Data for Predicting Distributions of Public Opinions

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the Wasserstein distance between the LLM's predicted public opinion distribution and the actual human survey response distribution across different age groups (e.g., 18-29, 30-49, 50-64, 65+).
Measuring the Wasserstein distance between the LLM's predicted public opinion distribution and the actual human survey response distribution across different genders (Male, Female).

Measuring the Wasserstein distance between the LLM's predicted public opinion distribution and the actual human survey response distribution across different racial and ethnic groups (e.g., Black, White, Asian, Hispanic).

Measuring the Wasserstein distance between the LLM's predicted public opinion distribution and the actual human survey response distribution across different income brackets and educational attainment levels.

Measuring the Wasserstein distance between the LLM's predicted public opinion distribution and the actual human survey response distribution across different political affiliations (Democrat, Republican) and ideologies (Liberal, Conservative, Moderate).

Measuring the Wasserstein distance between the LLM's predicted public opinion distribution and the actual human survey response distribution across different religious identities (e.g., Protestant, Jewish, Hindu, Atheist, Muslim).

Measuring the Wasserstein distance between the LLM's predicted public opinion distribution and the actual human survey response distribution across different US regions (Northeast, South, Midwest, West).
